title: C/C++ firmware repository: target boundaries, a host harness, a proven twin
subtitle: Use case walkthrough. Numbers from tools/golden_path.py on example-system/firmware-repo/
footer: Synthetic firmware tree. No customer data. No C-to-Python translator is offered.

slides.title: Three kinds of code in every firmware tree
bullets: Portable logic: parsers, filters, checksums, state machines - testable on a laptop
Target-only: ISRs, memory-mapped registers, startup, linker sections, inline assembly
Vendor and HAL: code you did not write and should wrap, not port
Before modernising anything: which is which, where the HAL seam is, what depends on what
A Python model, where wanted, is a behavioural twin proven against the C - not a translation

slides.title: The lane, step by step
rows: entry points, target-only files and markers, seam candidates, order
firmware-map.md, host-tests/ with stubs on the seam
one bounded pack per unit; manifest
/tdd host-test the unit, then the Python twin
tests + code, make test green, compare.md

slides.title: Fixture: 30 files that look like real firmware

stats.label: include edges + call edges; 1 unresolved, 4 indirect, 6 vendor calls

slides.note: ISR, registers, volatile, linker script, #if board variants, function pointers, C++ templates and overloads, vendor code, K&R legacy, a non-UTF-8 file. python tools/c_fleet_scan.py --check compares with expected/.

slides.title: Classification and seams
left: retain: ISR, inline asm, memory-mapped registers, linker symbols or sections, startup code
wrap: vendor / third-party, HAL-bound, includes a target-only header
unreadable: could not be read or parsed - listed, not dropped
right: A function in a retain / wrap file that host-side code calls
That is where the stub goes in templates/host-harness
gcc -MM cross-checks includes when gcc exists; its errors are reported verbatim
Without board flags the fixture reports: error: #error "unknown board"

slides.title: The finished twin in example-system

stats.label: tests pass on the C firmware (src/) and on the Python twin (sim/)
host-harness checks against the C through hal_stub.c

slides.note: Same tests, both implementations. The Python is an executable specification and host oracle, not a port.

slides.title: What this does not prove
bullets: Macros not expanded, #if not evaluated, function pointers not followed: edges are candidate evidence
C++ overloads, templates, virtual dispatch are matched by name only
Host tests prove logic on a laptop, not timing or interrupt behaviour on the target
No C-to-Python translator exists here; if translation is the requirement, say it is a gap

slides.text: Find the seam, test on the host, keep a twin honest with the same vectors. Everything target-only stays where it is, and the map says why.
